cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, has been bringing the LORD's word to Israel (Amos 1:1). Now he calls out to some women on Mount Samaria, and he calls them cows of Bashan, a land known for its cattle. Friend, Amos does NOT warm up the crowd first.

cards.question: Amos says these women on Mount Samaria oppress and crush people. Who are they oppressing and crushing?

cards.text: And they tell their husbands, "Bring us more to drink." Then the Lord GOD swears an oath, and He swears it by His holiness.

cards.question: The Lord GOD swears by His holiness about these women of Samaria. What does He say is coming for them?

answers.text: They will be taken away with hooks
They will be crowned in Samaria
They will be given more land

cards.text: Hooks for them, He says, and fishhooks for their posterity.

cards.question: When these women are taken away, the LORD says they will go out through broken walls.

cards.text: The LORD says each one will go straight ahead and be cast out toward Harmon. Then He names Bethel, where He already said He'd bring destruction on the altars (Amos 3:14), and Gilgal.

cards.question: The LORD sends Israel to Bethel and to Gilgal. What does He tell them to do there?

cards.text: And He keeps going: "Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days." EVERY THREE DAYS, friend, and I can't even remember to dust my gold base that often.

cards.question: Along with leavened bread as a thank offering, the LORD tells Israel to keep their freewill offerings quiet.
All those sacrifices, tithes and loud offerings. Why does the LORD say the children of Israel keep it all going?

answers.text: It's what they love to do

cards.text: Now the LORD lists what He brought on Israel, one thing after another. First: cleanness of teeth in all their cities and lack of bread in all their towns.

cards.question: After the LORD brought lack of bread on all of Israel's towns, how does He say Israel responded?

answers.text: They did not return to Him
They returned to Him in tears
They cried out to Him for help

cards.text: In the LORD's words: "…yet you did not return to Me…" Next, He withheld the rain when the harvest was three months away.

cards.question: When the LORD held back the rain from Israel, He held it back from every city and every field alike.

cards.text: One field got rain while the next one withered. People staggered from city to city for water to drink.

cards.question: Going from city to city, the people of Israel found enough water to be satisfied.

cards.text: That line again, friend: "…yet you did not return to Me…" Next, the LORD struck their growing gardens and vineyards with blight and mildew.

cards.question: On top of the blight and mildew, the locust devoured Israel's fig and olive trees.

cards.text: And again: "…yet you did not return to Me…" Then it gets heavier, friend: the LORD says He sent plagues among them.

cards.question: The LORD says the plagues He sent among Israel were like the plagues of which land?

cards.text: He says He killed their young men with the sword, along with their captured horses. This part is heavy.

cards.question: Plagues and the sword came on Israel. What does the LORD say He filled their nostrils with?

cards.text: And STILL: "…yet you did not return to Me…" Now the LORD brings up two cities He once overthrew.

cards.question: The LORD says He overthrew some of Israel the same way He overthrew which two cities?

cards.text: The LORD tells them they were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze. And for the fifth time: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

cards.question: After everything He brought on Israel, the LORD says He will do this to them. Then what does He tell Israel to do?

cards.text: Then the words turn to who this God is. He forms the mountains and He creates the wind.

cards.question: The God who forms the mountains and creates the wind keeps His thoughts hidden from people.
This same God turns the dawn into darkness.

cards.text: He strides on the heights of the earth. "…the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name."
